MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 13, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order City Clerk
Kimberly Schmitt at 5:08 p.m., on December 13, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 8, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

COUNCIL RELATED CEREMONIAL ITEM

1.  Administration of Oaths of Office

  The Oath of Office was presented to Wendy Bucknum by her husband Paul and Pastor Mike
  Maiolo, to Brian Goodell by the City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt, to Trish Kelley by her husband
  Jack, to Bob Ruesch by his wife Debbie, and to Cynthia Vasquez by her husband Alan Ooka.
  City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt presented Certificates of Election to Council Members Goodell,
  Bucknum, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez.

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

City Council Meeting Minutes  1  December 13, 2022
 CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION FOR 2023

2.  Selection of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2023

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley to
  appoint Brian Goodell to serve as Mayor in 2023.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Ruesch, to appoint Trish
  Kelley, as Mayor Pro Tem for 2023.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Brenda Cooper, M.V.: Encouraged the City Council to stay conservative and keep our community
family oriented. She stated that the same people continue to complain and she doesn’t understand
it. She thanked Cynthia for stepping up and being a Council Member.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Congratulated both Cynthia Vasquez and Bob Ruesch and suggested to them
that they question the suggestions and advice from the City Attorney. He criticized the previous
City Council for extending their terms and the cost of attorney fees. He outlined potential future
lawsuits and claims. He requested the two new Council Members ask for and publish the full
accounting Mr. Curley spent on legal matters to keep the five Council Members in office.

Wendy Lee, M.V.: Welcomed the new City Council. She looks to move forward away from any
division. She thanked both former Council Members Greg Raths and Ed Sachs for their service
and contribution to Mission Viejo.

Michelle O’Brien, M.V.: Stated that she loves our City and all that it has to offer. She thanked the
previous Council Members for all their hard work. She recognized Greg Raths and Ed Sachs for
serving the City and representing Mission Viejo. She looks forward to working with the City
Council and has faith that our City will continue what other Cities try to achieve.

Mary Wathen, M.V.: Commented on all the negative rhetoric this past year and believes it is time
to move on and to appreciate all the hard work done by our City Council . She noted that the
majority of residents of Mission Viejo as evident in the November 8 Election are in favor of this
Council. She thanked the Council for all they do, have done, and will do in the future.

City Council Meeting Minutes  2  December 13, 2022
 OLD BUSINESS

3.  Resolution Ratifying all City Council Actions Relating to the Implementation of the
  November 8, 2022 Election Results

  City Attorney Curley gave the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell to adopt
  Resolution 22-44 Confirming and Ratifying the Acts of the City Council of the City of
  Mission Viejo, California, at Both the Special Meeting and Regular Meeting Held on
  December 13, 2022, at 4:30 pm and 5:00 pm, and All Actions Conducted and Voted Upon
  in the Special Meeting and initial Portion of the Regular Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Labor Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6(a):
  Agency Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Keith
  Rattay; City Attorney William Curley; Director of Administrative Services Cheryl
  Dyas; Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz; and Labor Attorney Peter Brown:
  Employee Organization: Service Employees’ International Union (SEIU)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:33 p.m., City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt recessed the meeting. The City Council
reconvened at 6:08 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced no actions were taken, the Council was updated on
negotiations with the SEIU union. There will be an action on item 20 on what was discussed on
Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PUBLIC COMMENTS (Continued)

Smitha Shaker, M.V.: Congratulated the new members of the City Council. She agrees that it is
time to move on. She asked that people look at both sides of every argument. She asked that the
City Council move forward together. She commented on the recent Christmas Celebration and
City Council Meeting Minutes  3  December 13, 2022
 criticized Wendy Bucknum for serving as a representative of the City at this event, but they
excluded Cynthia at this event. Asked that the Council represent everyone in the City.

Ed Maurer, M.V.: Congratulated the new City Council. Stated he was surprised that the City has
not put into action the adoption of the Solar App+ Platform that he thought would be online in
January. He pointed out all the other Cities that have applied for grants and questioned why the
City has not looked into the grants. He hopes that the new City Council will get real about climate
change and apply for a Solar App+ grant now before the money runs out.

Ken Golemo, M.V.: Presented photographs regarding Eucalyptus trees in his neighborhood and
asked about the maintenance of the trees. He stated that they installed solar panels and there is an
increase in his electric bill due to the large Eucalyptus tree behind his home.

George Deltoro, M.V.: He spoke on security within the City and stated his house was burglarized
in Canyon Crest. He questioned if there could be more enforcement at Flo Jo Park after dark. He
asked if the fire road could have an easement that home owner’s association could put some
security equipment such as night cameras to protect those homes that back up to the park.

Bob Breton, M.V.: Congratulated Mayor Goodell and honorable Council Members. Thanked the
Council Members for their tireless efforts on our behalf to improve the quality of life that we enjoy
in Mission Viejo. He saluted former Mayor Bucknum for that way in which she carried the City’s
banner with dignity and grace with total commitment and deep devotion during the past year and
gave her many kudos. He also thanked the City Manager. Assistant City Manager, and all staff.

Council Member Goodell announced that as a point of personal privilege and respect for our
former Mayor, he asked Council Member Bucknum to chair the rest of tonight’s meeting.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez*
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None
*Council Member Vasquez abstained from item 4 – City Council Minutes.

4.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the minutes for the Regular Meeting of November 8, 2022, as presented.

5.  Check Register Dated October 28, 2022 in the Amount of $1,280,476.23

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated November 4, 2022 in the Amount of $1,235,038.05

City Council Meeting Minutes  4  December 13, 2022
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Check Register Dated November 14, 2022 in the Amount of $2,952,002.74

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Check Register Dated November 18, 2022 in the Amount of $1,568,036.33

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

9.  Check Register Dated November 25, 2022 in the Amount of $1,270,312.51

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

10. City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2022

  Received and filed.

11. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for October 2022

  Received and filed.

12. Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for October 2022

  Received and filed.

13. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October
  2022

  Received and filed.

14. Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Project (TRAP): Catch Basin Debris
  Screen and Automated Retractable Screen Installations in the Northerly Area (CIP
  23253)

  Awarded a construction contract in the amount of $200,000 to G2 Construction, Inc. for the
  Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Project (TRAP): Catch Basin Debris Screen
  and Automated Retractable Screen Installations in the Northerly Area

15. Montanoso Recreation Center Rehabilitation (CIP 314) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
City Council Meeting Minutes  5  December 13, 2022
   Faithful Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days, respectively,
  after the date of the Notice of Completion recordation and contingent upon the absence of
  claims or liens being filed with the City; (4) approved the second amendment to Nadar, Inc.
  for the Montanoso Recreation Center Rehabilitation - CIP 314; (5) authorized a change
  order to the existing purchase order for Nadar, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $3,937.00;
  and (6) authorized the payment of the final retention of $45,794.80, thirty-five (35) days
  after the date of the Notice of Completion recordation.

16. Coronado Park Play Area Rehabilitation (CIP 328) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $32,599.94,

17. Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park Field Lighting (CIP 331) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $34,966.36,
  thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion

18. Procurement of General Banking Services

  (1) Rescinded current City Council Policy 300-5 Rotation of Banking Services and (2)
  adopted proposed City Council Policy 300-5 Procurement of General Banking Services.

PUBLIC HEARING

19. Ordinance Adopting the 2022 California Building and Fire Codes, the International
  Swimming Pool and Spa Code and the International Property Maintenance Code.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Council Member Bucknum opened the Public Hearing at 6:47 pm. There being no requests
  to speak Council Member Bucknum closed the Public Hearing at 6:47 pm.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley to (1) adopt
  Ordinance 22-346 Adopting by Reference the 2022 Editions of the California Building,
  Residential, Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Green Building Standards, Historical
  Building, and Existing Building Codes, and the 2021 Editions of the International Swimming
  Pool and Spa Code and International Property Maintenance Code, Together, with Certain
City Council Meeting Minutes  6  December 13, 2022
   Appendices and Amendments Thereto, and Amending Title 8 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code"; (2) adopt Resolution 22-45 Setting Forth Findings for Required Amendments to the
  2022 California Building Code Relative to Local Climatic, Topographic, and Geologic
  Conditions; (3) adopt Ordinance 22-347 Adopting by Reference the 2022 California Fire
  Code, Together with Certain Amendments and Deletions"; and (4) adopt Resolution 22-46
  Setting Forth Findings for Required Amendments to the 2019 California Fire Code Relative
  to Local Climatic, Topographic, and Geologic Conditions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

20. Ratification of a Side Letter Agreement Between the City of Mission Viejo and SEIU
  Local 721

  Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Kelley to (1) adopt
  Resolution 22-47 Ratifying a Side Letter Agreement between the City of Mission Viejo and
  SEIU Local 721; and (2) adopt Resolution 22-48 Amending the City's Salary Schedule to be
  Effective Retroactive to July 1, 2022 and Effective January 1, 2023.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

CITY MANAGER REPORT

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon gave an update on the I-5 Widening project.

Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay updated the Council that the Church got all their permits in
and they will be moving into the Mart. He announced there will be a Night Market event this
weekend with Whoville and Santa’s Village and there will be a shuttle going back and forth from
City Hall. He also indicated that the Fire Station is getting close to submitting plans for the
temporary station and start construction sometime in February.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Curley announced that at the first meeting in January we will be asking the City
Council to give us direction amending the ordinance regarding commissions. Decision on whether
the commissioners have to reside in the same district as a Council Member, terms of office, .and
any other enhancements to the commissions will be discussed. He outlined the timeframe would

City Council Meeting Minutes  7  December 13, 2022
 be the first reading of the ordinance at the second of meeting in January with the adoption at the
first meeting in February.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch stated that he attended the Veteran’s Day Ceremony, Santa’s Arrival and
the Winter Gala. He thanked the many voters that elected him. He also thanked his wife Debbie.
Council Member Ruesch thanked his campaign team, Bob Breton, Peter Molinari, his son Andrew,
and Andie Lofy and most certainly the volunteers Lisa, Connie, Brian, Gary, and Michelle. Lastly,
he thanked Dennis Heyburn for being his lifelong friend and his support. He wished everyone a
Merry Christmas.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez thanked her husband and stated it was quite the experience running for
City Council and they both learned a lot and that she is very grateful to have him by her side. She
commented that she is very proud of going through this experience and showing her daughters that
if you really put in the effort and perseverance whether you win or lose. She explained that she
met many people that she would never have had the opportunity had she not run for office. Council
Member Vasquez said she is looking forward to working with the community throughout the City.
She thanked all her volunteers and the voters that elected her. She looks forward to learning from
the City Council. She clarified that on her vote for Mayor Pro Tem was to have one of the new
incoming Council Members serve as Mayor Pro Tem into that rotation. She asked the City
Attorney if she could get the status of the current litigation with the previous City Council and the
motion for attorney fees and costs. She also asked when the resolution for the City Manager
authority will be rescinded.

City Attorney Curley responded that the motion for attorney’s fees are being addressed. As far as
the Appeal, the record was filed in November. The documents are being prepared. He stated that
the City Manager authority resolution will be rescinded at the first meeting in January.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley stated it was a busy month. She commended City Staff, particularly Leslie
McDonald and Colonel Lundgren for the Veteran’s Day Ceremony and thanked the residents that
attended. She pointed out the success of Santa’s Arrival and Workshop and thanked the Mission
Viejo Activities Committee for putting on these events every year. Council Member Kelley stated
she attended two Ribbon Cutting Ceremonies, Gemma’s Jewelers and the Airforce Recruiting
Office. She attended the following events: Chamber of Commerce Mixer, Winter Gala, and
SCAG Economic Summit. This evening she announced is the Adopted Marines Battalion

City Council Meeting Minutes  8  December 13, 2022
 Christmas Party at Camp Pendleton and thanked all the residents that contributed gifts. She
thanked the voters and volunteers and welcomed Council Member Vasquez and Council Member
Ruesch. Lastly, she wished everyone a Merry Christmas, Happy Hanukah, and Happy Holidays to
everyone.

Council Member Goodell

Thanked those that supported him for reelection and the Council for selecting him as Mayor for
2023. He stated he is excited for the new year. Council Member Goodell thanked his wife Vicky.
He stated attended many events this last month. He thanked the Greg Raths, Ed Sachs and Wendy
Bucknum for their service to our community. Council member Goodell welcomed the new
councilmembers and looks forward to a fresh start in 2023. Lastly, wished everyone a Happy
Holiday.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum echoed what her fellow Council Members said before her and thanked
the voters. She stated in spite of the negative campaign signs she was still reelected with the
highest percentage of votes. She commented that her uncle earned a Life Time Achievement
Award from the Academy of Music in Hawaii. Council Member Bucknum thanked her husband,
Mission Viejo Christian Church, and Assemblywoman Kate Sanchez. She gave a big shout out to
her volunteers, Lisa, Sandy, Steve, Tricia, and Victoria as her Treasurer. Council Member
Bucknum also thanked her neighbor Karen who she could also call in the middle of the night. She
thanked her son for putting together signs. Council Member Bucknum thanked Sherri Butterfield
for stepping up tonight to certify the election and she deserved a lot more respect than the negative
comments this evening from the public. Without Sherri Butterfield there would be no Library.
She spoke on the Housing Element and suggested that we may have to establish a special
subcommittee to handle getting this squared away and the other things that may come with it
including a specific plan in the appropriate locations. She informed that there will be a State of
the City beginning of next year. She recapped the progress on a lot of issues such as, Sober Living
Homes, public safety, increase of public input, civic core progress, paving along Oso Creek Trail,
and the golf course improvements. Council Member Bucknum stated she wants to work
cooperatively together with the City Council. Lastly, she thanked Greg Raths and Ed Sachs for
their service to the City.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:38 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this special
meeting, Council Member Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of Dennis Lumley.

Approved at the meeting of January 10, 2023
